cells.tense: The heart here is open, and nothing has been poured into it yet.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Toward a goal you are moving on, let the pull arrive first — no plan, no pick. Afterwards, one line about what drew you.
cells.core:
You can hold a direction and stay undecided about it at the same time. Aimed at something, the heart is already ajar, with no label closing the gap and nothing specific landing in it — and that is what lets a person show you who they are rather than who the goal needs them to be. Both of you stay whole in it. Nothing merges.
Most people cannot keep a goal this close and still be open. That is the strength here. Notice what draws you before you pick a heading, and give the pull a moment to steer. The aim may shift once you feel what is actually there, and that is not failure — that is the goal getting truer. What you understand keeps deepening instead of shutting.
cells.sheetLine: You can stay open toward a goal before you name it.
cells.verb: keeping the heart open before anything is poured
cells.place: where momentum is aimed at a destination

cells.tense: Where momentum is pointed, the ending is felt before the beginning has arrived.
cells.act: finish the legacy by sustained will
cells.ask: Pick a goal you have been pushing at, write what finished looks like, call it closed for now — then leave it untouched for a week.
cells.core:
Toward a destination, the heart is opening early and filling with what has not happened. The ending gets felt first — anticipation, prep, wanting arriving well before the thing itself. It reads as dedication from where you stand. From the other side it reads as a heart that will not sit still long enough to take anything in. Nothing arrives on the schedule it would have kept, because you are already there waiting.
Close one. Take a single goal, name what done looks like in a sentence, set that down as the end, and stop steering it for seven days. What stays open after that can be received at whatever pace it sets. Direction that comes from clarity holds; direction that comes from bracing does not, and the week will show you which one you were running on.
cells.sheetLine: You brace for the finish before you've taken the start.

cells.tense: The opening was there before, and the heart has been treating it as a door already past.
cells.act: complete what you began by beginning it
cells.ask: Take up something you started and dropped — small counts. Begin it again from the first step, one sitting, no catching up.
cells.core:
Readiness comes easily to you — the heart opens before there is anything to feel about, and it does that unbidden. What has gone quiet is the direction. A person can be open toward a goal and still not move, and after enough of that, the open moment reads as one that was missed. What is missing is not effort. It is the beginning. The spark has been waiting for you to come back to it, not for more pressure pushed into the blank.
Begin one of those old starts over, from the very first step, as though for the first time. No catching up, no reckoning with the gap. Just the beginning, done once, while it is still small. What you began will tell you what it is for, and the current runs through the starting, not through a fresh push.
cells.sheetLine: The door opened. You're standing past it.

cells.tense: The heart is open and taking things in now, and the taking goes on someone else's account.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: Name a recent gift of yours that got nothing back. Ask for a return of the same size, and when it comes, count it as yours.
cells.core:
Toward what you are moving toward, you receive first and file it under luck, or under their idea, or under timing. The openness is yours — the thing that lets another person's direction land in you and change your aim. Yet when you look at what moved, the credit sits somewhere else, and you stay out of your own account. The heart that opened is the one whose name is missing from the page.
An exchange is running here, and you are only on one side of it. Give something and take something back, the same size, from someone in it with you. Not a favour owed and not a tally — one return, allowed to belong to you. Watch what happens when it arrives and you do not hand it to circumstance.
cells.sheetLine: You're open to what comes, and you don't count it as yours.
